newsitem.title: USA: Supervalu gets $305 mln from ShopKo stake.
newsitem.headline: Supervalu gets $305 mln from ShopKo stake.

text.p: Supervalu Inc said Wednesday it had received $305 million in net proceeds from two transactions through which it sold its 46 percent stake in ShopKo Stores Inc, a regional discount retailer.
Supervalu said it received about $155 million, net of estimated underwriting expenses, from a secondary public offering of 6,557,280 ShopKo shares.
It also received $150 million from selling 8,174,387 shares directly to ShopKo.
As previously announced, Supervalu repurchased 6.9 million shares of its common using proceeds from the two transactions.

Supervalu said it bought six million of the shares from a financial intermediary, subject to a market price adjustment provision. In order to complete the deal, the financial intermediary borrowed Supervalu common shares and will be purchasing replacement shares in the open market.

Supervalu said that while it has 60.5 million shares outstanding, its board previously authorized the repurchase of 1.6 million shares. It will consider additional purchases from time to time, it said.
Future earnings per share will benefit from the reduced shares outstanding, it added.

Supervalu said it estimated that using proceeds from the ShopKo transaction for share repurchases will have a minor dilutive effect on fiscal 1998 earnings per share, and will be additive in future years.

"The completion of the two ShopKo transactions supports our strategic plans to focus on food businesses and to enhance shareholder value," Mike Wright, Supervalu chairman, said in a statement. "In that regard, we are also pleased to be able to convert the non-cash earnings from ShopKo into cash which is being returned to our shareholders, following directly after our 26th consecutive dividend increase."
Supervalu is a food distributor and the 13th largest food retailer in the U.S.
